full_text:
Chandigarh Weather: चंडीगढ़ में चार डिग्री तक गिरेगा तापमान, सुबह-शाम बढ़ेगी ठंडक
चंडीगढ़ में अक्टूबर के अंत तक तापमान में 4 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरावट आने की संभावना है, जिससे सुबह और ...और पढ़ें
HighLights
अक्टूबर अंत तक तापमान में 4 डिग्री गिरावट संभव।
सुबह और रात के समय ठंडक में वृद्धि होगी।
अगले पांच दिन मौसम साफ, दिन में धूप खिलेगी।
जागरण संवाददाता, चंडीगढ़। अक्टूबर के विदा होने में अब केवल पांच दिन शेष हैं और चंडीगढ़ में ठंड का असर भी धीरे-धीरे बढ़ने लगा है। सुबह और रात के समय मौसम ठंडा रहने लगा है। आने वाले दिनों में ठंडक और बढ़ने की संभावना है।
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, अगले कुछ दिनों में अधिकतम तापमान में चार डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरावट दर्ज की जा सकती है। इससे दिन के समय भी मौसम पहले के मुकाबले ठंडा महसूस होगा।
मौसम विभाग ने अगले पांच दिनों तक मौसम साफ रहने का अनुमान जताया है। आसमान साफ रहने के कारण दिन में धूप खिली रहेगी, लेकिन तापमान में गिरावट से सुबह और रात की ठंडक बढ़ सकती है। ऐसे में लोगों को दिन और रात के तापमान में अंतर महसूस होगा।
सुबह घर से निकलने वाले लोगों को ठंड का सामना करना पड़ सकता है, जबकि दोपहर में धूप के कारण मौसम अपेक्षाकृत सामान्य बना रहेगा। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, रविवार को शहर का अधिकतम तापमान 31.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया।
यह सामान्य से 1.7 डिग्री सेल्सियस अधिक रहा। वहीं, न्यूनतम तापमान 16.9 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जो सामान्य से 2.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस कम रहा। न्यूनतम तापमान में आई गिरावट से रात के समय ठंडक बढ़ने का एहसास हो रहा है।
आने वाले दिनों में बदलेगा मौसम का मिजाज
अक्टूबर के अंतिम सप्ताह में तापमान में गिरावट के साथ मौसम का मिजाज बदलने लगा है। हालांकि, फिलहाल बारिश की संभावना के बजाय मौसम साफ रहने का अनुमान है। अधिकतम तापमान में गिरावट होने से दिन की गर्मी से राहत मिल सकती है। वहीं, न्यूनतम तापमान में और कमी आने पर सुबह और रात के समय ठंड का असर बढ़ सकता है। मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, अगले पांच दिनों में तापमान में होने वाला बदलाव शहर में सर्दी की शुरुआत का एहसास करा सकता है।

title: Anambra First Lady Urges Precautions Against Heatstroke - Voice of Nigeria

full_text:
Anambra State First Lady, Dr Nonye Soludo, has urged Nigerians to adopt preventive measures against extreme heat, warning that rising temperatures pose public health risks, particularly to children, older people and persons living with chronic illnesses.
Soludo, wife of Governor Chukwuma Soludo and Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Healthy Living with Nonye Soludo, gave the advice in a public health message, calling for increased awareness of heat-related illnesses and practical steps to protect vulnerable populations.
“As we head deep into a period of increased heat, I encourage every family to take simple but important precautions to protect their health,” she stressed.

She advised Nigerians to drink sufficient water, wear light clothing, avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight and keep their homes well ventilated to reduce the risk of heat-related illnesses.
Soludo specifically urged families to pay attention to older people, babies and persons living with hypertension, diabetes or kidney disease, noting that these groups might be more vulnerable to complications associated with extreme heat.
A heatwave is a prolonged period of unusually high temperatures that can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially fatal heatstroke. Extreme heat can also worsen existing conditions, including heart and kidney diseases, placing additional pressure on individuals, families and healthcare services.
The health risks underscore the importance of public education, early recognition of symptoms and access to timely medical care, particularly in communities where safe drinking water, adequate ventilation and healthcare services may be limited.
Soludo encouraged Nigerians to check regularly on vulnerable relatives and neighbours, especially during periods of intense heat, to identify signs of illness and ensure prompt assistance.
“Also, check on your loved ones, especially in the mornings and evenings. If anyone shows signs of severe heat illness, move them to a cool place, begin cooling their body, and seek emergency medical attention immediately,” she advised.
Warning signs of heat exhaustion include heavy sweating, weakness, dizziness, headache and nausea. Heatstroke is a medical emergency that may cause confusion, seizures or loss of consciousness and requires immediate emergency assistance and rapid cooling while medical help is on the way.
The Anambra First Lady also advised parents and caregivers never to leave children in parked vehicles and urged people to limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest periods of the day.
She called for sustained public health education to help households recognise heat-related risks and adopt preventive practices, stressing that timely intervention and simple precautions could reduce avoidable illnesses and deaths.
“Anambra’s Emergency Line is still 112. Remember that a little caution today can save a life tomorrow,” Soludo reminded residents.
The advisory highlights the need for coordinated public health awareness as communities face periods of high temperatures. Health education, access to safe drinking water, appropriate housing and ventilation, and responsive emergency services are important measures for reducing heat-related health risks across Nigeria.

title: Heavy rain alert: Deep depression to intensify into cyclone on Monday - India Today

Rain alert for Andhra, Odisha: Bay of Bengal depression to intensify into cyclone
A Bay of Bengal deep depression is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast. Odisha has activated evacuations, closures and disaster teams as heavy rain threatens vulnerable districts.
A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday morning and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday, October 28, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall across Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall across Odisha from October 27 to 29 as the weather system approaches the eastern coast. Odisha has stepped up preparations, with Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi deputing eight ministers to vulnerable districts and mobilising disaster response teams.
The system is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam around the forenoon of October 28, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, officials said.
The projected landfall area is around 300 km from Odisha's Gopalpur.
RED ALERT FOR FIVE ODISHA DISTRICTS
The Odisha government has issued a red alert for Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri for October 28, as these districts are likely to bear the brunt of the approaching cyclone.
The districts could receive heavy to very heavy rainfall, with isolated extremely heavy downpours exceeding 20 cm. The rainfall is likely to be accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty surface winds reaching 60-70 kmph, the IMD said.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said the weather system could affect southern and coastal Odisha with heavy rainfall and gusty winds of 70-90 kmph. Significant rainfall is also expected in other coastal areas.
SCHOOLS SHUT IN FIVE DISTRICTS
The Odisha government has ordered the closure of all schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri on October 28 and 29.
Collectors in other districts will decide on closing educational institutions depending on how the weather situation evolves.
Majhi has directed officials to shift people from vulnerable areas to safer locations, with particular attention to elderly people, patients and pregnant women. Those requiring medical assistance should be moved to healthcare facilities if necessary.
The chief minister reiterated the state's zero-casualty objective and asked officials to prioritise public safety, evacuation and emergency response.
60 ODRAF, 17 NDRF TEAMS DEPLOYED
Odisha has positioned rescue teams from the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and the Fire Services in vulnerable areas.
"Around 60 ODRAF teams and 17 NDRF teams have been deployed, while 225 Fire Services teams are on high alert," Majhi said.
Collectors in coastal and southern districts have been directed to keep cyclone shelters ready for people who may need to be evacuated.
Ganjam District Collector Keerthi Vasan V said 100 cyclone shelters had been kept ready and 1,000 temporary locations identified to accommodate people if evacuation becomes necessary.
The chief minister has also directed departments, including Health and Family Welfare, Water Resources, Energy, Agriculture, Panchayati Raj, Rural Development and engineering services, to remain prepared and promptly repair any damage caused by the cyclone and associated rainfall.
EIGHT MINISTERS ASSIGNED TO VULNERABLE DISTRICTS
Majhi has deputed eight ministers to oversee preparedness and response measures in vulnerable districts. They will remain in their assigned districts from October 27 to 29, officials said.
Deputy Chief Minister K V Singh Deo has been assigned Koraput, while Deputy Chief Minister Pravati Parida will oversee arrangements in Rayagada.
Rural Development, Panchayati Raj and Drinking Water Minister Rabi Narayan Naik has been assigned Kandhamal, while Commerce and Transport Minister Bibhuti Jena will oversee preparations in Ganjam.
Food Supplies and Consumer Welfare Minister K C Patra will be in Nabarangpur, School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond in Malkangiri, Higher Education Minister Suryabanshi Suraj in Gajapati and Health Minister Mukesh Mahaling in Kalahandi.
Senior officials experienced in handling extreme weather events have also been assigned responsibilities in vulnerable districts. They include K Sudarshan Chakravarthy in Rayagada, Poma Tudu in Koraput, Bijay Kumar Dash in Gajapati, Yedula Vijay in Malkangiri and Maheshwar Swain in Nabarangpur.
In a separate order, the state government cancelled the leave of all district collectors, district magistrates and other officers posted in critical offices. They have been directed to return to their respective headquarters immediately to ensure administrative readiness.
FISHERMEN ADVISED NOT TO VENTURE INTO SEA
The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the sea from October 24 in view of the developing weather system.
The weather department has also advised that Distant Cautionary Signal No-I (DC-1) be hoisted at all ports in Odisha.
Majhi said that although the system is forecast to make landfall in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh, Odisha will remain fully prepared to deal with any eventuality.

full_text:
The IMD has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in five Keralam districts on Sunday and Monday.
Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad districts are under red alert on October 25, while Idukki and Palakkad are under red alert on October 26, according to the IMD's latest update.
An orange alert has been issued for Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod on Saturday, indicating the possibility of very heavy rainfall in isolated areas.
Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki and Ernakulam are under yellow alert for heavy rainfall on the day.
The India Meteorological Department defines extremely heavy rainfall as precipitation exceeding 204.4 mm in 24 hours, very heavy rainfall as 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm and heavy rainfall as 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm during the same period.
In view of the alerts, the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) warned that intense rainfall over a short period could trigger flash floods, overflowing streams, waterlogging in urban and low-lying areas, landslides and landslips.
The KSDMA advised people in landslide-prone hilly areas and flood-prone low-lying regions to move to safer locations if necessary. It also urged people not to cross rivers or enter water bodies during heavy rain, avoid non-essential travel and stay away from waterfalls and hilly areas until the warnings are withdrawn.
Night travel to hilly areas should be completely avoided, the KSDMA said in a Facebook post, urging the public and government agencies to remain vigilant.
Published on October 24, 2026

title: Tamil Nadu Rain Alert: Five Districts Under Red Alert - Urban Acres

full_text:
Tamil Nadu’s early northeast monsoon intensified on October 25, with five districts placed under a red alert and several others receiving an orange alert as heavy rain flooded roads and landslides were reported in parts of the Nilgiris, according to a report by Dinamalar.
Pudukkottai, Thanjavur, Ariyalur, Perambalur and Tiruchirappalli were listed under a red alert for the day. The Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Tiruppur and Dindigul were among the districts placed under an orange alert for very heavy rainfall.
The weather system has affected several districts over the past few days, with the report stating that the northeast monsoon began earlier than usual and has since intensified. Landslides were reported at several locations in the Nilgiris, while heavy rain in Coimbatore, Tiruppur and Dindigul caused floodwater to run across roads.
Rainfall recorded until 8.30 pm showed the highest total at Othakkal Mandapam in Coimbatore, where 15.2 centimetres was recorded. Karathozhuvu in Tiruppur received 13.1 cm, while Madathupalayam in Erode recorded 11 cm.
Other significant rainfall totals included 10.6 cm at Nallampalayam in Tiruppur, 8.7 cm at Varapatti in Coimbatore, 8.6 cm at Kolathupalayam in Tiruppur and 8.5 cm at Appiyampatti in Dindigul. Vellalur in Coimbatore recorded 8.4 cm, while Paruthiyur in Dindigul received 8 cm.
The report also recorded 7.8 cm at both Dharapuram in Tiruppur and Pakkiripalayam in Villupuram. Thondamuthur in Coimbatore received 7.6 cm, followed by Kodaikanal in Dindigul with 7.4 cm and Kannivadi in Tiruppur with 7.1 cm.
Rainfall was also reported across the Nilgiris, Ramanathapuram, Cuddalore and other districts. Konavakkarai in the Nilgiris recorded 5.9 cm, Edappalli received 5.6 cm, and Kengarai and Kodanadu recorded 5.52 cm and 5.4 cm respectively. Mandapam in Ramanathapuram recorded 5.6 cm, while Nellikuppam in Cuddalore received 5.3 cm.
The distribution of rainfall highlights the pressure placed on roads and settlements across both western and central Tamil Nadu. Floodwater on roads can disrupt local travel, while landslides in hill districts create additional risks for road access and hillside communities. The alert designations and rainfall observations reported on October 25 remain the immediate indicators for residents and local authorities as the northeast monsoon continues.

The IMD Telangana rain forecast has placed Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem and Khammam under a red alert for October 28, with extremely heavy rainfall expected in isolated areas as a weather system develops over the Bay of Bengal.
The India Meteorological Department’s Hyderabad office said rainfall activity is likely to increase across the State from Tuesday, October 27, after a prolonged dry spell. Heavy rain is expected at isolated places on Tuesday, while the most intense conditions are forecast for Wednesday.
The red alert covers areas where heavy to very heavy rainfall, including isolated extremely heavy downpours, is likely on October 28. The IMD has also warned of thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds as the weather system approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast.
An orange alert has been issued for Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Mahabubabad and Suryapet districts. These areas are expected to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on October 28. Other districts in Telangana may also receive heavy rain, according to the forecast.
The weather system is expected to produce continuing unsettled conditions on October 29. The IMD has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places, along with thunderstorms and lightning in parts of the State. The department’s warning covers a period when sudden downpours and gusty winds could affect road travel, outdoor activity and local services in the districts under alert.
The district-level warnings are particularly relevant for eastern Telangana, where Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mahabubabad and neighbouring areas have been identified in the alert categories. The forecast does not indicate that every location within these districts will receive extreme rainfall, as the warning refers to isolated areas.
The IMD said residents should monitor official weather bulletins as the system develops because rainfall warnings may be updated. Local authorities and residents in the red- and orange-alert districts will need to follow subsequent advisories on thunderstorms, lightning, strong winds and heavy rain through October 29.
